title: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death
hook: Karna has Yudhishthira beaten, and lets him go
carry: either way you'll keep your sons
tomorrow: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death

segments.voice: Yesterday, Karna heard Shalya's story of the crow and the swan, and rode on anyway. Where did you try one way, done straight? Day eight hundred thirty-nine.

Yudhishthira's bow is cut. His chariot is wrecked. He is the eldest of the Pandavas, the man the whole war is being fought to crown, and he is beaten, standing within reach of Karna's weapons. One more arrow would do it. Karna's army would cheer. Duryodhana would have the war in his hand. And Karna lowers his weapon. He mocks Yudhishthira, tells him to go back to his own kind and leave fighting to warriors, and he lets him go. In the epic he spares Nakula, one of the twins, the same way. Today, why.
screen: `YUDHISHTHIRA IS BEATEN.` → `ONE MORE ARROW.` → `KARNA LETS HIM GO.`

segments.voice: The answer is back before the war, by a riverbank. Karna used to pray facing the sun, and one day, as he finished, a woman was standing in his shadow. It was Kunti, the mother of the Pandavas. And she told him what he had never known for certain: she was his mother too. She had borne him as a girl, before her marriage, a son of the sun god, and set him afloat on the river. Now she asked him to come over to his brothers' side. Karna refused. Where were you, he says in effect, when I needed a mother? Duryodhana stood by me when no one else did, and I won't leave him now. But he gave Kunti something. He promised he would not kill her sons, except Arjuna. One of the two of us will die, he told her, and either way you'll keep your sons. So on the field, with Yudhishthira at his mercy, Karna remembers the riverbank. And here's the part that aches. The brothers don't know. To Yudhishthira, Karna is the enemy who humiliated him and inexplicably let him live. Karna knows, and Kunti knows, and so does Krishna, who had told him of his birth. The brothers don't know that they are being spared by their own brother.
screen: `KUNTI AT THE RIVERBANK` · `I WON'T LEAVE DURYODHANA` · `A PROMISE TO HIS MOTHER` · then, large: `THE BROTHERS DON'T KNOW`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your shoulders drop. Breathe in, and breathe out slowly. Bring to mind a promise you're carrying that nobody else can see, something you've agreed to hold for someone. Don't weigh whether it's easy. Just hold it, the way you'd hold something fragile in both hands. Breathe in, and feel its weight. Breathe out, and let your hands stay steady. If you pray, you can bring that promise into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Karna. The warrior who could have ended the war with one arrow, and kept a promise to his mother instead, while his brothers never knew why.
Your line: either way you'll keep your sons. Today, keep one small promise that nobody will ever thank you for. Day eight hundred thirty-nine.

howItsDone: The meeting of Kunti and Karna by the river is retold in readings, plays and poems, and Karna's choice to stay with Duryodhana is discussed in Hindu homes and classrooms as a hard question about loyalty and duty.

myth: Karna agreed to join his brothers once Kunti told him the truth
he refused; he would not leave Duryodhana.
Karna promised Kunti not to kill her sons, except Arjuna
and on the field he keeps that promise.
Yudhishthira knew why Karna spared him
the brothers didn't know Karna was their brother.

fork.setup: you're Karna. Yudhishthira stands beaten in front of you, and one arrow would end the war. what do you do?
options: mock him, and let him go.
fork.reveal: Karna mocks him and lets him go, keeping the promise he made to Kunti by the river.

original.note: Kunti: mother of the Pandavas, and, in secret, of Karna.

trapdoor: what you thought: Karna went easy on Yudhishthira out of contempt.
what it means: he was keeping a promise to his mother not to kill her sons, except Arjuna.
what a scholar hears: the mockery and the mercy arrive together, so the brothers read only the insult; the epic lets the reader know more than the people in the story.

notes: Editor pass: softened 'Only Karna, Kunti and Krishna know' (others in the epic, such as Bhishma, also know) to name who knows without claiming they are the only ones.
All paraphrase. Confirm in the Karna Parva that Karna defeats and spares Yudhishthira and Nakula, with mocking words, and that the text ties this to his promise to Kunti.
The hook's paraphrase of Karna's taunt (go back to your own kind, leave fighting to warriors) should be checked against Ganguli.

Confirm the riverbank details: Karna praying facing the sun, Kunti standing in his shade, his reply about her abandoning him, and the promise that she will still have her sons with either Karna or Arjuna. The count 'five' was deliberately left out.
Some retellings put the sparing of Sahadeva and Bhima in the Drona Parva; the script names only Yudhishthira and Nakula.

Audit: 'Then ... he does the same with Nakula' put Nakula's sparing after Yudhishthira's; in the Karna Parva Karna defeats and spares Nakula earlier. Reworded without a sequence. Keeper: confirm placement.
